references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "Among those born of women, no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he."
Jesus speaks about the privilege the disciples have to see and hear what the prophets and the righteous longed for, which explains why the least in God's kingdom is greater than John.

The angel Gabriel prophesies about John's greatness—that he will be great before the Lord and go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah. This supports Jesus' statement that no one born of women is greater than John.
Zechariah prophesies that John will be called a prophet of the Most High and go before the Lord to prepare his ways. This confirms John's unique role among those born of women.
Malachi prophesies about the messenger who will prepare the way for the Lord—a prophecy fulfilled through John the Baptist, highlighting his greatness among the prophets.
The expression "born of women" (γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν) reflects Job's wording concerning human frailty and limitation, which Jesus also uses to describe the human sphere to which John belongs.
Here too, the expression "born of a woman" is used regarding humanity's condition, which Jesus draws upon when describing John as the greatest among those born of women.

Jesus speaks about some who are last becoming first, and that people from all directions will sit at the table in God's kingdom—this highlights the theme that the least in God's kingdom hold an exalted position.

Peter writes that the prophets searched and investigated the salvation that was to come, but it was not for themselves they served. This explains why the least in God's kingdom is greater than John—they have seen its fulfillment.
